nodes.title: Parcel Desk knowledge
nodes.body:
# Parcel Desk knowledge

A small **fictional** pickup service. The vault has two layers. The **as-built spec** says what the code does today and is derived only from source. The **gap queue** holds every question about what is missing, doubtful or proposed; people re-check and decide each one. This is a worked example, not a production readiness assessment.

## The spec

Read it as one document in [AS-BUILT](AS-BUILT.md) (generated), or page by page:

- **[[areas/pickups|Pickup cancellation]]** covers the state transition and the response mapping.
- [[areas/access|Customer access]] covers whose pickup can be changed.

Start with [[notes/cancellation-boundary|the cancellation boundary]], then [[notes/route-responses|the route response mapping]]. The rule in [[notes/ownership-check|Customer ownership]] runs first.

## The gap queue

[GAPS](GAPS.md) (generated) lists every gap by state. In this example:

- [[gaps/packed-cancellation|Packed cancellation]] is accepted, with [[plans/packed-cancellation|a plan]].
- [[gaps/partner-decision|Partner cancellation]] has been rechecked and awaits a person's decision.
- [[gaps/deployment-evidence|Deployment evidence]] has not been rechecked yet.

See [[01-coverage|Coverage]] and [[runs/example-survey|the example survey]] for limits. `AS-BUILT.md` and `GAPS.md` appear after `build`; open `graph.html` in a browser or `Map.canvas` in Obsidian for the map.

nodes.title: Coverage and evidence limits
nodes.body:
# Coverage and evidence limits

Return to [[00-index|the index]].

## Pickup coverage

In [[areas/pickups|Pickups]], the service, adapter and all three tests were read. Three existing unit tests passed; none uses a `packed` pickup. Real HTTP responses, concurrent writes and persistent state are outside the fixture.

## Access coverage

In [[areas/access|Access]], the owner guard and the denied-action test were read. The test shows another customer's requested pickup is refused without a state change. Authentication, partner identities and deployed authorization are outside the fixture.

The release check ran `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` from the fictional project: **PASS, 3 tests**. That result says nothing about packed pickups; the open question is [[gaps/packed-cancellation|packed cancellation]].

## Limits

The source fingerprints describe this shipped fixture. There is no reviewed Git checkpoint embedded in the example because it is a subdirectory of the toolkit, not an independent application repository. Copy the fixture into a temporary Git project before trying incremental commit sync.

No real service, logs or customer data were inspected. That does not imply those systems are missing from an actual product; [[gaps/deployment-evidence|deployment evidence]] records the boundary as a gap.

nodes.title: Customer access
nodes.body:
# Customer access

The adapter accepts a customer identifier supplied by its caller, and the service compares it with the pickup's owner before looking at state. This is a policy check on a supplied value; nothing in the fixture authenticates a request.

- [[notes/ownership-check|Ownership rule]] constrains [[areas/pickups|pickup cancellation]].
- [[notes/route-responses|Route responses]] shows how a refusal is reported as status 403.

Read: [service](../../../src/pickups.py), [adapter](../../../src/routes.py), and [tests](../../../tests/test_pickups.py). The other-customer test passed in the example check. Identity providers, sessions and any partner identity are not present in the fixture.

nodes.title: Pickup cancellation
nodes.body:
# Pickup cancellation

This area covers the in-memory cancellation transition and the adapter response built from it. It depends on [[areas/access|customer access]], whose owner check runs before any state is considered.

- [[notes/cancellation-boundary|Cancellation boundary]]: the service cancels only pickups whose state is `requested`.
- [[notes/route-responses|Route responses]]: service exceptions become status values.

Read: [service](../../../src/pickups.py), [adapter](../../../src/routes.py) and [tests](../../../tests/test_pickups.py). The three existing tests passed in the example check. Not modeled: real transport, persistence, concurrent requests and deployment.
nodes.summary: How a customer's pickup is cancelled in the in-memory service and how the adapter reports the outcome.

nodes.title: What do an allowed and a denied cancellation return through a real entrypoint?
nodes.body:
# What do an allowed and a denied cancellation return through a real entrypoint?

## Current behavior

Cancellation runs as in-process Python calls: `cancel_request` returns dictionaries and takes an already-authenticated customer string. See [[notes/route-responses|the response mapping]] and [[notes/ownership-check|the owner check]].

## Gap

The [requirements](../../../SPEC.md) describe an in-memory fixture with no network server, identity provider or database. Nothing here shows what a real deployment returns. When an allowed and a denied cancellation go through a deployed entrypoint, do they produce the same responses and state changes as the in-process calls?

## Evidence

- Documented boundary: the "Boundary" section of [SPEC.md](../../../SPEC.md) says the fixture has no network server, identity provider, database or provider integration; the module docstring of [routes.py](../../../src/routes.py) says the same of the adapter.
- No deployment checks were run (NOT RUN). For this fictional example there is nothing to run.

## Recheck

Not checked yet.

## Discussion

- 2026-11-14 · agent: In an actual project the next step would be to name the real entrypoint and environment, then test one allowed and one denied cancellation. Authentication, persistence and concurrent cancellations would each be a separate gap. For this example the gap marks the limit of what the vault can claim.

## Decision

Open.

nodes.title: Should a customer be able to cancel their own packed pickup?
nodes.body:
# Should a customer be able to cancel their own packed pickup?

## Current behavior

The service cancels only `requested` pickups and rejects every other state, including `packed`, after the owner check; the adapter reports that as status 409. See [[notes/cancellation-boundary|the cancellation boundary]], [[notes/ownership-check|the owner check]] and [[notes/route-responses|the response mapping]].

## Gap

CAN-1 in [the requirements](../../../SPEC.md) says a customer can cancel their own pickup before collection, "including when its state is `requested` or `packed`". The code does not do that for `packed`. Should the service change so the owner can cancel a packed pickup?

## Evidence

- Documented intent: CAN-1 in [SPEC.md](../../../SPEC.md).
- Static reading: the state guard in [cancel_pickup](../../../src/pickups.py) permits only `requested`; [cancel_request](../../../src/routes.py) maps the resulting `ValueError` to 409.
- The three existing [tests](../../../tests/test_pickups.py) pass and none uses a `packed` pickup, so they neither show nor contradict the mismatch.

## Recheck

2026-11-15, Tomas Brandt: ran `cancel_request(Pickup("example", "customer-a", "packed"), "customer-a")` in the fixture. Result: `{'status': 409, 'error': 'cancellation_conflict'}` and the state stays `packed`. The same call with `customer-b` returns 403 and also leaves the state unchanged. Confirmed against the current files; this is a local in-process call, not a request to a deployed service.

## Discussion

- 2026-11-14 · agent: Found while mapping the cancellation flow. The alternative to changing the code is revising CAN-1 to say `requested` only.
- 2026-11-15 · Priya Nair: CAN-1 stays as written; support has had packed-pickup complaints. The partner question is separate and does not block this.

## Decision

Accepted on 2026-11-15 by Priya Nair: keep CAN-1 and change the service. Planned in [[plans/packed-cancellation|the implementation plan]].

nodes.title: Should a delivery partner be able to cancel on a customer's behalf?
nodes.body:
# Should a delivery partner be able to cancel on a customer's behalf?

## Current behavior

Only the pickup's owner can cancel: the service compares the supplied customer ID with the owner, and the adapter takes a customer identity and nothing else. See [[notes/ownership-check|the owner check]] and [[notes/route-responses|the response mapping]].

## Gap

DEC-1 in [the requirements](../../../SPEC.md) leaves partner cancellation undecided and outside the accepted scope. Does the product want it? If so, who may act for whom, what identity evidence is required, and in which states?

## Evidence

- Documented intent: DEC-1 in [SPEC.md](../../../SPEC.md) says permissions, identity checks and allowed states "have not been decided".
- Static reading: [cancel_request](../../../src/routes.py) has no partner parameter, role or contract.
- Nothing was run: the fixture defines no partner behavior to run.

## Recheck

2026-11-15, agent: re-read [SPEC.md](../../../SPEC.md) and [routes.py](../../../src/routes.py) (static only). DEC-1 is still undecided in the requirements and the adapter still has no partner path, so the description above still holds (confirmed). The proposal itself is not judged here; that is for the person deciding. No command was run.

## Discussion

- 2026-11-14 · agent: Absence of a partner path is not a missing accepted feature. Options for a decider: (a) reject for now, (b) defer until a partner integration exists, (c) accept and define permissions, identity checks and states first.

## Decision

Open.

nodes.title: Only requested pickups are currently cancellable
nodes.body:
# Only requested pickups are currently cancellable

Area: [[areas/pickups|Pickup cancellation]]. Use this note when changing allowed states or explaining a rejected cancellation.

`cancel_pickup` first runs the [[notes/ownership-check|ownership check]]. It then requires `pickup.state == "requested"`; any other value, including `picked_up` and `packed`, raises `ValueError("Only requested pickups can be cancelled")` before anything is changed. A pickup that passes both checks gets state `cancelled` and is returned. The [service](../../../src/pickups.py) establishes this; the code has no list of states and treats every value except `requested` the same way. The service refers to no other state name.

The [[notes/route-responses|adapter]] turns the `ValueError` into status 409. The existing [tests](../../../tests/test_pickups.py) cover a `requested` pickup (cancelled) and a `picked_up` pickup (409, unchanged); none uses `packed`. The three-test suite passed during the example check (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, see [[01-coverage|coverage]]).

nodes.title: The owner check runs before the state check
nodes.body:
# The owner check runs before the state check

Areas: [[areas/access|Customer access]] and [[areas/pickups|Pickup cancellation]].

`cancel_pickup` compares `pickup.customer_id` with the supplied customer ID before it looks at the state. A mismatch raises `PermissionError` and nothing is changed; the adapter maps it to status 403 ([service](../../../src/pickups.py), [adapter](../../../src/routes.py)). The only caller identity in the code is that supplied string: the adapter's docstring says the caller has already authenticated the customer, and no partner or staff identity exists.

`test_other_customer_cannot_cancel` in the [tests](../../../tests/test_pickups.py) uses a `requested` pickup and checks status 403 and unchanged state; it passed in the example check. [[notes/cancellation-boundary|State eligibility]] applies only after this check passes.

nodes.title: Cancellation exceptions become adapter statuses
nodes.body:
# Cancellation exceptions become adapter statuses

Areas: [[areas/pickups|Pickup cancellation]] and [[areas/access|Customer access]].

The in-process `cancel_request` adapter calls `cancel_pickup` and returns a dictionary: `{"status": 403, "error": "forbidden"}` for `PermissionError`, `{"status": 409, "error": "cancellation_conflict"}` for `ValueError`, and `{"status": 200, "state": <new state>}` on success. See [the adapter](../../../src/routes.py) and [the called service](../../../src/pickups.py).

[[notes/ownership-check|Ownership]] decides the 403 case and [[notes/cancellation-boundary|state eligibility]] decides the 409 case, so a `packed` pickup owned by the caller reaches the 409 branch. The [existing tests](../../../tests/test_pickups.py) exercise the three branches with a requested, an other-customer and a collected pickup, and passed in the example check. The values are dictionaries returned in-process, not observed HTTP responses.

nodes.title: Plan: allow the owner to cancel a packed pickup
nodes.body:
# Plan: allow the owner to cancel a packed pickup

Implements [[gaps/packed-cancellation|the accepted gap]]. This is a plan only; nothing here has been implemented or run.

## Current behavior

`cancel_pickup` permits only `requested` ([[notes/cancellation-boundary|cancellation boundary]]), after the [[notes/ownership-check|owner check]], and the adapter reports a refusal as 409 ([[notes/route-responses|response mapping]]).

## Steps

1. In [tests/test_pickups.py](../../../tests/test_pickups.py), add a packed-pickup check through `cancel_request` expecting status 200 and state `cancelled`. Run it first and confirm it fails with the current 409.
2. In [src/pickups.py](../../../src/pickups.py), accept `requested` and `packed` and keep the owner check before any state change. Keep every other state rejected.
3. Add regression cases: a packed pickup with the wrong customer returns 403 and stays `packed`; a `picked_up` pickup returns 409 and stays `picked_up`. Keep the existing requested case.
4. Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` from the fixture root. After the new behavior is verified, update the cancellation notes from the code and mark the gap `done` with the location of the change.

## Acceptance

- The owner can cancel `requested` and `packed` pickups: status 200, state `cancelled`.
- Another customer receives 403 and the state is unchanged.
- A `picked_up` pickup receives 409 and the state is unchanged.

All of these are proposed checks: **NOT RUN**.

## Out of scope

Partner cancellation (see [[gaps/partner-decision|its gap]], still undecided), persistence, HTTP integration, and the behavior of cancelling an already cancelled pickup.

nodes.title: Fictional project survey
nodes.body:
# Fictional project survey

This authored example surveys the four fixture source, requirements and test files. It is not a transcript of an independent agent run. The fixture has no independent application revision: it ships inside the toolkit repository, whose Git commit identifies the exact version.

## 2026-11-14: survey

Wrote the [[areas/pickups|pickup]] and [[areas/access|access]] maps and three behavior notes from the code. Raised three gaps, each with `decision: "open"`: [[gaps/packed-cancellation|packed cancellation]] (the code rejects a state the requirements allow), [[gaps/partner-decision|partner cancellation]] (the requirements leave it undecided) and [[gaps/deployment-evidence|deployment evidence]] (not checkable in this fixture). Ran `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` from the fictional project: **PASS, 3 tests**. Reviewed source fingerprints were then accepted; view generation does not make claims true.

## 2026-11-15: gap queue

Tomas Brandt rechecked packed cancellation by running the fixture; Priya Nair accepted it and [[plans/packed-cancellation|a plan]] was written. The agent rechecked partner cancellation by reading the code and left the decision open. Deployment evidence has not been rechecked. No spec note changed.

See [[00-index|the index]] and [[01-coverage|coverage]]. No external system was queried and no real product behavior is implied. Release checks and browser observations are in the toolkit's `VALIDATION.md`.
